links.outcome: Cumulative regret, false negative rate, and accuracy of bandit-governed adaptive model selection versus static and other strategies
links.effect: Across 3,000 simulated ICU admissions, the bandit framework had lower cumulative regret than static, random, ensemble, and heuristic switching; lower false negative rates; comparable overall accuracy.
links.quote: Across 3,000 sequential ICU admissions, adaptive deployment governed by the multi armed bandit framework achieved lower cumulative regret than static single model deployment, uniform random selection, ensemble averaging, and heuristic switching strategies.

links.outcome: Performance stability across age and sex subgroups under bandit governance versus static deployment
links.effect: Bandit governance exhibited more stable performance across age and sex subgroups relative to static deployment.
links.quote: The governance layer also reduced mean operational cost per prediction and exhibited more stable performance across age and sex subgroups relative to static deployment.

unlisted_practices: Contextual multi-armed bandit adaptive model selection among candidate models with delayed outcome feedback and composite reward including safety penalties and operational cost
